releaseNote.summary: Concurrent updateData requests on a parked Busy instance now continue the chain once; hosts name their Postgres connections (Application Name).

migrations.title: Parked Busy continuations are claimed once per state
migrations.description: Before: when several updateData requests found an instance parked in Busy (an interaction wait with no live owner), every one of them took the parked pipeline over and ran the automatic chain again — duplicate parent notifications and finalize calls, and a stale Status=B written back over the settled state. Now a continuation first claims the instance with one set-based UPDATE on the new nullable column Instances.ContinuationClaimedAt (Status='B' AND CurrentState unchanged AND no claim younger than 60 s); the winner runs the chain and clears the claim, a loser drops its continuation and logs 10182 (UpdateDataContinuationClaimLost). The claim does not move modifiedAt. Every host also adds Application Name (OTEL_SERVICE_NAME, else DAPR_APP_ID, else the host name) to a Postgres connection string that has none, so pg_stat_activity and PgBouncer SHOW CLIENTS name the owning host.
migrations.action: Run DbMigrator before rolling out the hosts (it adds the nullable column). No configuration change is required; a connection string that already sets Application Name is left as it is.
